changes.before: If the print calls trade places, which text result appears first?
changes.after: A program is a set of instructions for a computer. R follows these print instructions from top to bottom.

before: R evaluates instructions in order. print displays a representation of a value.
Double quotes mark text, called a character value. In print("Moon"), parentheses hold the value supplied to print, which displays that text.
In the ordinary R console display, [1] marks the position of the first displayed element. It is a display label, not part of your text.
print normally shows quotes around character text. Two print calls produce two displayed results in order.
Expected result: [1] "Moon" followed by [1] "River" on another line. Follow the instructions in order; this is a worked example, not an in-app execution.
after: A program is a set of instructions for a computer. R follows these print instructions from top to bottom.
The quotes mark the text values Moon and River.
Print displays the value. The [1] in the output marks the position of the first item on that printed line.

Follow the labeled parts of this example.
```r
print("Moon")
print("River")
```
The output is `[1] "Moon"`, then `[1] "River"`. The first call shows Moon. The second call shows River.
Swap the two calls on paper and follow the new order.
